source.title: High Voltage Direct Current Power Supply Market to Reach USD 695.01 Million by 2034 as Data Centre Infrastructure Expands
source.body:
Global High Voltage Direct Current Power Supply Market was estimated at USD 320.00 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 348.80 million in 2026. According to Energy Resources Insights, the market is expected to reach USD 695.01 million by 2034, representing an assumed compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.0% during 2026–2034. Market development is supported by increasing data centre electricity requirements, telecommunications infrastructure expansion and demand for efficient power conversion technologies. Asia-Pacific represents the largest regional market under the report's analyst scenario.

High voltage direct current (HVDC) power supply system’s convert alternating current into regulated direct current for applications requiring stable and reliable electrical power. The market covers 240 VDC and 380–400 VDC conversion equipment, including rectifier cabinets, distributed modular conversion systems and associated power distribution controls. These systems serve data centres, telecommunications facilities and industrial applications requiring continuous electrical operation.

Market at a Glance

2025 market size: USD 320.00 million
2026 estimate: USD 348.80 million
2034 forecast: USD 695.01 million
Forecast CAGR: 9.0% during 2026–2034
Leading region: Asia-Pacific, with an indicative 49% share of 2025 revenue.
Key applications: Data centres, telecommunications, industrial and other critical loads.

Data Centre Expansion and Efficient Power Conversion Drive Growth

The increasing use of cloud computing, artificial intelligence and digital services is creating substantial electricity requirements across data centre infrastructure. Operators are evaluating power distribution technologies that can improve electrical efficiency, reduce conversion stages and support high-density computing environments.

Traditional data centre power infrastructure commonly uses alternating-current distribution and multiple conversion stages before electricity reaches IT equipment. High-voltage DC architectures offer an alternative by supplying regulated direct current through dedicated rectification and distribution equipment.

The ability to reduce certain conversion stages can improve overall electrical-system efficiency. Higher-voltage DC distribution can also reduce current requirements for a given power level, influencing cable sizing and distribution design. These characteristics make the technology relevant to large computing facilities and telecommunications installations.

Telecommunications infrastructure provides another source of demand. Network facilities require dependable power systems capable of supporting continuous communication services. Centralized rectifier cabinets and modular conversion systems can help operators manage electrical loads and maintain power availability.

Industrial applications also contribute to market opportunities, particularly where critical equipment requires stable DC power. However, adoption depends on equipment compatibility, protection coordination, maintenance expertise and the economics of replacing established AC and UPS architectures.

The market remains dependent on application-specific engineering. Existing infrastructure, server power-supply compatibility, electrical safety requirements and available technical support influence purchasing decisions.

Key Market Drivers and Challenges

Several factors are shaping the industry's outlook:

Data centre expansion: Increasing computing capacity and digital infrastructure investment support demand for high-capacity DC power conversion systems.
Artificial intelligence workloads: High-density computing environments encourage evaluation of advanced power distribution architectures.
Telecommunications infrastructure: Network expansion and continuous service requirements create opportunities for reliable DC power systems.
Energy efficiency requirements: Reduced conversion stages and optimized electrical distribution can improve system-level energy performance.
Modular power architecture: Distributed conversion and modular rectifier cabinets offer flexibility for infrastructure expansion and replacement projects.

The market also faces challenges. Transitioning from established AC power infrastructure requires investment in compatible equipment and protection systems. Existing facilities may face retrofit costs, while maintenance personnel require specialized training. Equipment interoperability, fault protection, system reliability and availability of spare parts also influence adoption.

Segmentation and Regional Outlook

The market is segmented by power system type, application, architecture and installation.

By type: 240 VDC Power Systems, 380–400 VDC Power Systems.
By application: Data Centres, Telecom, Industrial and Other Critical Loads.
By architecture: Centralized Rectifier Cabinets, Distributed Modular Conversion.
By installation: New Build, Replacement and Retrofit.

Asia-Pacific leads the market with an indicative 49% share of 2025 revenue under the report's analyst scenario. The region benefits from expanding digital infrastructure, telecommunications investment and increasing data centre capacity. China, Japan, India and South Korea represent important markets for advanced electrical infrastructure.

North America accounts for an indicative 25% of 2025 revenue, supported by data centre development, cloud computing infrastructure and demand for reliable power systems. Europe represents approximately 19%, with opportunities associated with digital infrastructure modernization and energy efficiency initiatives. The Middle East & Africa and South America account for indicative shares of approximately 4% and 3%, respectively.

These regional percentages are analyst scenario estimates rather than audited supplier revenue statistics.

Competitive Landscape

The competitive environment includes manufacturers of DC power conversion equipment, telecommunications power systems and data centre electrical infrastructure. Vertiv has documented commercially available 400 VDC rectifier systems, including cabinet configurations designed for high-capacity applications. Huawei has also described 240 VDC power architecture deployments in data centre environments.

Competition is influenced by power conversion efficiency, system reliability, modularity, output voltage, monitoring capabilities and integration with existing infrastructure. Suppliers are increasingly emphasizing scalable power solutions that can support growing computing and communication requirements.
